page: Microsoft Azure F2-1amds_v7 is an x86_64 server belonging to the Famdsv7 family. It features a dedicated AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, configured with 1 physical core and 1 vCPU. The virtual machine is equipped with 16.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per core. Local storage is provided by a 236 GB NVMe SSD, and the instance is premium storage capable. The hypervisor layer is managed by Microsoft Hyper-V.

Benchmark data highlights a stark contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Due to its single-core configuration, the server achieves top-tier single-core CPU performance in stress-ng and high single-threaded compression speeds, such as 40.79 GB/sec in gzip and 17.87 GB/sec in bzip3. However, multi-core CPU metrics and Passmark CPU scores fall into the weak category. Memory bandwidth is average for large blocks at 41.76 GB/sec read and 31.4 GB/sec write, but weak for small cached blocks. Static web serving throughput is poor at 2.65 GB/sec, and database operations or Redis SET operations also rank in the lower percentiles.

This server offers a specialized resource density profile, pairing a high-frequency single core with a generous 16 GB memory allocation and fast local NVMe storage. This makes it a qualitatively cost-efficient option for workloads that require significant memory capacity and fast local disk access but do not benefit from multi-threaded processing. The primary tradeoff is the strict limitation of a single vCPU, which severely restricts multi-threaded performance, parallel processing, and high-throughput web serving. Appropriate workloads include memory-intensive single-threaded applications, lightweight databases, caching layers, and basic text or prompt processing tasks.
